title: Adult cardiac arrest: basic and advanced life support (India)
specialty: Emergency Medicine / Critical Care / Cardiology / Anaesthesia

evidenceAudit.scope: In- and out-of-hospital adult cardiac arrest in India: high-quality cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), defibrillation, adrenaline and antiarrhythmics, reversible causes and post-resuscitation care, using the Resuscitation Council UK ALS algorithm (2025), the ERC 2021 ALS guideline (summary) and the AHA 2020 guideline, because no Indian national ALS guideline with doses could be opened.
findings: CPR 30:2, 2-minute cycles, pad change after 3 shocks, adrenaline every 3–5 minutes (first dose after 3 shocks in shockable rhythms), amiodarone after 3 shocks, waveform capnography, 4 Hs and 4 Ts, and post-return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) targets (SpO2 94–98%, normal PaCO2, systolic BP above 100 mmHg, 12-lead ECG, temperature control) checked against the RCUK Adult ALS algorithm (2025).

Adrenaline 1 mg IV/IO, amiodarone 300 mg then 150 mg, lidocaine 100 mg then 50 mg, biphasic first shock at least 150 J, three stacked shocks for monitored arrest, thrombolysis with CPR for 60–90 minutes if PE suspected checked against the ERC 2021 summary.
Compression rate 100–120/min and depth at least 5 cm, chest compression fraction at least 60%, ETCO2 at least 10 mmHg (ideally 20 mmHg) checked against AHA 2020.
unverifiedSections: ERC 2021 (summary) gives a 4-minute adrenaline interval; RCUK 2025 gives 3–5 minutes. Both are shown.
Doses are taken from a secondary summary of ERC 2021, not the full guideline text.
Paediatric life support is not covered (see Paediatric resuscitation topic when available).
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Cardiac arrest is the sudden loss of effective cardiac output. In adults it is most often caused by coronary disease and ventricular fibrillation (VF) or pulseless ventricular tachycardia (pVT), but in Indian hospitals hypoxia, sepsis, haemorrhage, hyperkalaemia, poisoning and pulmonary embolism are common causes. Survival depends on the chain of survival: early recognition and call for help, immediate high-quality CPR, early defibrillation for shockable rhythms, adrenaline, treatment of reversible causes (4 Hs and 4 Ts) and structured post-resuscitation care.
keyMechanisms: VF or pVT: chaotic or very fast ventricular activity with no output; defibrillation restores organised rhythm.
PEA or asystole: usually from a reversible cause such as hypoxia, hypovolaemia or electrolyte disturbance.
Chest compressions generate coronary and cerebral perfusion pressure.
Adrenaline raises coronary perfusion through alpha-adrenergic vasoconstriction.

symptoms: Preceding chest pain, breathlessness or palpitations in some
redFlags: Unresponsive with abnormal breathing: start CPR and call for help
Suspected PE: consider thrombolysis and continue CPR 60–90 minutes (ERC 2021)
Hyperkalaemia, poisoning, tamponade, tension pneumothorax: treat the cause

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Respiratory arrest with pulse; pinpoint pupils.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Unresponsive, not breathing normally, no pulse.
Hypoxia, hypovolaemia, hypo/hyperkalaemia and metabolic, hypo/hyperthermia; thrombosis, tension pneumothorax, tamponade, toxins.

clinicalManagement.title: Basic life support
actions: Call for help and a defibrillator; start CPR 30:2 (RCUK ALS).
Compressions 100–120/min, depth at least 5 cm, minimal pauses (chest compression fraction at least 60%) (AHA 2020).

clinicalManagement.title: Shockable rhythm (VF/pVT)
actions: Shock (biphasic first shock at least 150 J), then CPR for 2 minutes (ERC 2021; RCUK).
Monitored, witnessed arrest: up to 3 stacked shocks (ERC 2021).
After 3 shocks: adrenaline and amiodarone; change pads to antero-posterior (RCUK 2025).

clinicalManagement.title: Non-shockable rhythm (PEA/asystole)
actions: Adrenaline as soon as IV or IO access, then every 3–5 minutes (RCUK; ERC 2021).

clinicalManagement.title: Reversible causes
actions: Suspected PE: thrombolysis and continue CPR 60–90 minutes (ERC 2021).

clinicalManagement.title: After ROSC
actions: ABCDE; SpO2 94–98%; normal PaCO2; systolic BP above 100 mmHg (RCUK 2025).
Asystole over 20 minutes despite ALS with no reversible cause: consider stopping (ERC 2021).

medicationPlan.note: Adrenaline, amiodarone and lidocaine doses from the ERC 2021 summary; sequence and post-ROSC targets from the RCUK 2025 algorithm; CPR quality from AHA 2020. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

learningObjectives: Run the shockable and non-shockable pathways.
Treat reversible causes and manage ROSC.
keyPoints: Push hard and fast: 100–120/min, at least 5 cm.
Shock first for VF/pVT; 2 minutes CPR after each shock.
Adrenaline 1 mg; amiodarone 300 mg after 3 shocks.
pitfalls: Long pauses for rhythm checks or airway.
